requirements.data_requirements: The platform must store user profiles, problem data, submission history, and leaderboard information.

tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure code submission and evaluation works correctly.

T1.implementation_approach: Use a component-based design approach with a framework like React or Angular to create a user-friendly interface for browsing, searching, and filtering problems.
T1.notes: Focus on responsive design and accessibility.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop RESTful APIs to handle CRUD operations for problems, including endpoints for adding, updating, deleting, and retrieving problems.
T2.notes: Ensure proper validation and error handling.

T3.implementation_approach: Design a relational database schema with tables for problems, categories, and tags. Use indexing for efficient querying.
T3.notes: Normalize the database to avoid redundancy.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a form-based interface for users to submit code, with syntax highlighting and file upload support.

T5.implementation_approach: Implement a sandboxed environment to execute user-submitted code securely and compare outputs with expected results.
T5.notes: Ensure security and prevent malicious code execution.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a profile page to display user details, progress, and achievements using a card-based layout.

T7.implementation_approach: Develop APIs for managing user profiles, including endpoints for retrieving and updating user data.

T8.implementation_approach: Design a database schema for user profiles, including tables for user details, progress, and achievements.
T8.notes: Ensure scalability for a large number of users.

T9.implementation_approach: Create a leaderboard interface with sorting and filtering options to display top users based on scores.

T10.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to fetch leaderboard data, calculate rankings, and update scores dynamically.

T11.implementation_approach: Design an interface to display hints and solutions for problems, with collapsible sections for better user experience.
T11.notes: Ensure hints are displayed progressively to avoid spoilers.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop APIs to manage hints and solutions, including endpoints for retrieving and updating them.

T13.implementation_approach: Perform unit and integration testing for the problem library functionality using test cases for all CRUD operations.

T14.implementation_approach: Test the code submission and evaluation system with various edge cases and ensure secure execution.

T15.implementation_approach: Test user profile features, including data retrieval, updates, and progress tracking.
T15.notes: Focus on data consistency and accuracy.

T16.implementation_approach: Test leaderboard functionality, including sorting, filtering, and real-time updates.

T17.implementation_approach: Test hints and solutions functionality, including progressive hint display and access control for solutions.

T18.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform using a cloud service provider, set up CI/CD pipelines, and configure monitoring tools.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize the SQLAlchemy instance
db_instance = SQLAlchemy()

def db():
    """
    Returns the SQLAlchemy database instance.
    """
    return db_instance
# SQLAlchemy db instance for models
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<Problem {self.title}>'

from app.database import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f'<User {self.username}>'

from app.database import db

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.now())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.now(), onupdate=db.func.now())
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, nullable=False)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, nullable=False)

    def __init__(self, code, language, problem_id, user_id):
        self.code = code
        self.language = language
        self.problem_id = problem_id
        self.user_id = user_id

    def save(self):
        db.session.add(self)
        db.session.commit()

    def delete(self):
        db.session.delete(self)
        db.session.commit()

from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_blueprint
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_blueprint
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_blueprint

def register_blueprints(app):
    """
    Register all blueprints to the Flask app instance.
    """
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app.routes import problem_blueprint, user_blueprint, solution_blueprint

def create_app():
    # Create a Flask application instance
    app = Flask(__name__)

    # Configure the app (e.g., database URI, secret key, etc.)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///acm_platform.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize the database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints for routing
    app.register_blueprint(problem_blueprint, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_blueprint, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_blueprint, url_prefix='/solutions')

    return app

from app import create_app

app = create_app()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles and Progress Tracking: Enables users to create profiles, track their progress, and view their problem-solving history.
- Leaderboard: Displays a ranking of users based on their problem-solving performance and achievements.
- Hints and Solutions: Provides hints and detailed solutions for problems to help users learn and improve.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
